fill_instruction: Use the same study ID in both columns and every trial row.
Freeze the planned rules before collection and retain revisions.
Use a unique ID for each hardware/software/calibration configuration.
State the task-specific claim and the comparison it requires.
Name GelSight Mini or original DIGIT and the exact acquired revision; do not substitute Digit 360 or DIGIT Pinki.
Use a local identifier traceable to the sensor serial number.
Record acquisition code plus reconstruction/detector/policy versions and environment.
Record robot and hand/gripper revisions and controller configuration.
Record adapter and finger spacing plus cable clearance and contact coverage.
Record gel identifier/type and replacement/wear history plus the unloaded-image path.
Define task and object/material IDs; keep object identities in trial rows.
Define initial pose/contact/loading/speed/environment with units and tolerances.
Define allowed control/inference budget and any per-condition training or tuning.
Declare held-out objects/sessions/units and keep related sequences together.
Set repeat counts and randomization/counterbalancing before outcomes are known.
Define end-to-end success including time limit and required dwell time if applicable.
Define operator/controller interventions and their effect on the success decision.
Define invalid-trial reasons in advance; retain excluded rows and reasons.
Separate raw RGB observations from derived depth/force/slip; state each claimed unit.
Link a versioned calibration record to each trial; use not_applicable with a reason for raw-only acquisition.
Identify reference geometry or force measurement and its own calibration/evidence.
Record calibration range and independent validation contacts/objects/loads.
Define error metric and units plus reference uncertainty and repeated-contact variability.
Define saturation/missing/corrupt/out-of-range observations; do not replace them with zero.
Record width x height and requested FPS plus encoding/exposure/lighting; these are settings.
Define the counted frames and timestamp window; store measured rate per trial.
Define what counts as a gap and how it is measured; distinguish irregular timestamps from confirmed lost frames.
Identify timestamp origin and whether it marks exposure/capture/receive/publish time.
Name reference clock and clock-mapping method with residual timing uncertainty.
Define observable start and end events such as capture to controller command; state if actuator response is measured separately.
Choose per-trial mean/median/percentile/max and observation count; do not mix statistics.
Identify external reference and onset-label method independent of the tested detector; use not_applicable with reason for other tasks.
Define physical slip onset and annotation interval rather than treating detector output as truth.
Set matching window and one-to-one event matching; define early and duplicate alarms.
Define independently labeled non-slip time and exclusions for false-alarm reporting.
Report attempted/excluded/evaluable counts and define whether interventions count as failures.
Choose interval/resampling method and independent unit; summarize each condition and held-out group separately.
List differences that remain between devices and limit the comparison.
Record primary documentation revisions and paths to raw logs/calibration/annotations.
